drawing.fits: the whole of his afro, both shoes, both hands, both mallets and the whole marimba
drawing.look: tall, narrow, long-armed adult build, long thin lined face, neatly trimmed short beard flecked with grey, round gold-rimmed spectacles, focused gentle smile, brown skin, big perfectly round black afro, long-sleeved cream dinner jacket buttoned closed, its narrow midnight-violet satin lapels lying flat on the chest, a small midnight-violet bow tie at a closed cream shirt collar, slim dark charcoal trousers and polished two-tone cream and dark shoes, and thick dark ink outline, behind a compact wooden marimba with a row of coral-red rosewood bars at his waist and a row of brass resonator tubes hanging beneath them, on a dark frame with two end legs
drawing.extra: He is a grown man of about forty. He holds two separate short mallets, one in each hand, each as long as his forearm with a round cream head. The marimba stands between him and the viewer at the same angle as his body, about as wide as he is tall and staying in the same place: its row of bars crosses in front of his belt and covers his hips, and its brass tubes hang in front of his thighs, with his shins and both shoes showing below them.

front.description: standing square facing the viewer behind the marimba, feet apart, elbows out, looking down at the bars, the hand on the left of the picture lifted to shoulder height and the hand on the right of the picture low over the bars

front_3q.description: standing behind the marimba, seen in a three-quarter view from the side: the chest, hips, knees, toes and nose all point toward the lower right corner of the picture, the face in three-quarter view looking that way, playing out toward a crowd on that side, feet apart, looking down at the bars, the mallet in the hand on the left of the picture raised by his shoulder and the other mallet down on a bar
front_3q.extra: He is a grown man of about forty. He holds two separate short mallets, one in each hand, each as long as his forearm with a round cream head. The marimba stands between him and the viewer at the same angle as his body, about as wide as he is tall and staying in the same place: its row of bars crosses in front of his belt and covers his hips, and its brass tubes hang in front of his thighs, with his shins and both shoes showing below them. The marimba is turned the same way: its row of bars runs on a diagonal, its end on the left of the picture nearer the viewer, larger and lower, and its end on the right of the picture smaller and higher.
